findings.title: Data quality validation present
findings.evidence: Data is loaded and written onward with no validation checks in between; after `pd.read_csv(...)` the code सीधे writes to silver via `balances.to_csv(...)` and `movements.to_csv(...)` without any assert/filter/quality validation.

remediation.description: Add explicit data quality checks after loading the CSVs and before writing them to silver.
remediation.fix:
python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
path = Path('Treasury_Pipeline/01_IngestCashPositions.py')
text = path.read_text()
old = '''        balances = pd.read_csv("bronze/BankAccountBalances_20240701.csv")
        movements = pd.read_csv("bronze/DailyCashMovements_2024-07-01.csv")

        balances.to_csv("silver/BankAccountBalances_20240701.csv", index=False)
        movements.to_csv("silver/DailyCashMovements_2024-07-01.csv", index=False)
'''
new = '''        balances = pd.read_csv("bronze/BankAccountBalances_20240701.csv")
        movements = pd.read_csv("bronze/DailyCashMovements_2024-07-01.csv")

        assert not balances.empty, "balances must not be empty"
        assert not movements.empty, "movements must not be empty"
        assert balances.notna().all().all(), "balances contains null values"
        assert movements.notna().all().all(), "movements contains null values"
        assert len(balances) == len(balances.drop_duplicates()), "balances contains duplicate rows"
        assert len(movements) == len(movements.drop_duplicates()), "movements contains duplicate rows"

        balances.to_csv("silver/BankAccountBalances_20240701.csv", index=False)
        movements.to_csv("silver/DailyCashMovements_2024-07-01.csv", index=False)
'''
if old not in text:
    raise SystemExit('target block not found')
path.write_text(text.replace(old, new))
PY

findings.title: Shared output table grain documentation
findings.evidence: The repository documents a grain statement for every gold output and every Dim/Fact table. Gold output `gold/LiquidityForecast_20240701.csv` is described in `Treasury_Pipeline/03_ForecastLiquidity.py` as a per-account forecast (`forecast = movements.groupby("bank_account_id")...` and `logger.info("Gold forecast written: %d accounts", len(forecast))`), and the README says the gold layer is a "30-day liquidity forecast". The SQL DDL files define `Reporting.CounterpartyDim` and `Reporting.LiquidityForecastFact`; `Treasury_SQL/CreateLiquidityForecastFact.sql` explicitly states "one row per bank account per forecast day", and `Treasury_SQL/CreateCounterpartyDim.sql` is a dimension table definition for counterparty exposure tracking. No gold output or Dim/Fact table is missing a grain statement anywhere in the repository.
